heading: The region at a glance
text: Across Tunisia, Algeria, Morocco, Libya and Egypt, protected areas and OECMs cover 1,524,625 km², or 27.7% of the region's 5,505,680 km² of land, and 13,139 km², or 1.2%, of its 1,114,014 km² of sea. Two countries pass 30% on land, Algeria (54.3%) and Morocco (33.7%); none comes close at sea.

heading: OECMs carry the land figure
text: Protected areas alone cover 4.4% of the region's land. OECMs add 23.3 points, all of it from two countries: Algeria's five Saharan Cultural Parks (1,151,696 km²) and Morocco's permanent hunting reserves and SIBEs (131,066 km²). Tunisia, Libya and Egypt report no OECMs. Whether these areas meet the CBD criteria for OECMs (decision 14/8) is a national judgement that each report should document; their effectiveness evidence is thin.

heading: The sea is the regional gap
text: Marine coverage ranges from 0.07% in Algeria to 3.62% in Egypt. Reaching 30% across the region's waters would take another 321,065 km². No country has an OECM at sea of any size, and several marine protected areas (Morocco's Mogador, Alboran, Massa and Agadir) are still only proposed.

heading: Key Biodiversity Areas
text: The region's 255 KBAs are on average 42.7% covered, and 83 have no coverage at all. Mountain KBAs (95) are the least covered group, at 35.3% on average, with 32 uncovered, most of them in the Tell and Aurès ranges of northern Algeria. Marine KBAs (55) average 44.6%.

heading: Representation
text: Coverage follows the desert. Within Algeria, most Saharan ecoregions are 45–100% covered through the Cultural Parks, while across the region the Mediterranean woodlands and forests are about 12% covered and the Nile Delta under 1%. Freshwater habitats are poorly covered everywhere except the salt flats: marshes and river floodplains rarely exceed 20%.

heading: Governance and effectiveness
text: Almost all reported area is governed by national governments; the exception is Morocco, where 88% of covered land is reported as collaborative governance. Egypt has no governance type for 47.9% of its covered land. Effectiveness evidence is weak across the board: no evaluation in the region carries a score, and only a handful are less than five years old.

heading: Data gaps that change the numbers
text: Libya's WDPA holds five point sites while its strategy lists more than 40 declared reserves and wetlands; Egypt has 13 large protected areas proposed since 1999; Morocco has 42 proposed sites, including its new natural parks. Updating the WDPA would move every figure in this dashboard more than any methodological choice.

heading: How the numbers were made
text: Each country was processed with the same pipeline: WDPA and WD-OECM October 2026; proposed sites and UNESCO biosphere reserves removed; points buffered to circles of their reported area; land and sea measured in Mollweide equal-area projection; protected areas dissolved; OECMs measured after erasing protected areas. KBAs use the official polygons (September 2026); ecosystems use RESOLVE ecoregions and Marine Ecoregions of the World; inland waters use HydroRIVERS and GLWD v2. Each country's workbook was recalculated in Excel with zero formula errors.

heading: Summary
text: Protected areas cover 7.93% of Tunisia's land and 1.07% of its sea, close to the 7th National Report's 7.86% and 1.1%. Reaching 30% would take 34,340 km² more on land and 28,926 km² at sea. Most wetlands are listed twice, as a national wetland zone and as a Ramsar site, so flattening removes more than a third of the summed area.

heading: Ecosystems and inland waters
text: Coverage leans on the salt flats: Chott Jrid alone is 40% of protected land. Lakes and wetlands are 46.8% covered, mostly salt pans, while the Mediterranean woodlands and forests of the north are 2.3% covered.

heading: Key Biodiversity Areas
text: The 72 KBAs average 41.4%; only 2 are fully covered and 22 have none, including the Gafsa steppe and Jbel Zaghouan.

heading: Governance and effectiveness
text: Nearly all covered land is government-governed. Only Ichkeul has an evaluation from the last five years (World Heritage Outlook 2025), and none has a score.

heading: What would move the figure
text: Designating the north's forests and Mediterranean coast, and adding marine protected areas around the Zembra, Kerkennah and Kuriat islands, would address the weakest parts of the network.

heading: Summary
text: Algeria covers 54.32% of its land: 4.65% in protected areas and 49.67% in five Saharan Cultural Parks reported as OECMs. The sea is at 0.07%, 39,342 km² short of 30% and about 6,500 km² short of the national 5% target.

heading: The OECM question
text: The Cultural Parks protect cultural and natural heritage together. Their OECM status rests on Algeria's own reporting; each has one METT assessment from 2011. A report should give the protected-area and OECM figures separately.

heading: Ecosystems and inland waters
text: The Saharan ecoregions are well covered through the Cultural Parks; the Mediterranean woodlands and conifer forests of the Tell are 13% and 9% covered, with no OECM contribution. Salt pans are 85% covered, marshes 15%.

heading: Key Biodiversity Areas
text: The 65 KBAs average 43.5% (35.1% by protected areas alone). Mountain KBAs average 22.7%, and the largest uncovered areas are Aurès–Chélia, the Dahra and Monts des Traras.

heading: Governance and effectiveness
text: The Tassili n'Ajjer World Heritage site and Djebel Aïssa National Park have no governance type, leaving 6.0% of covered land unreported. Its 2025 World Heritage Outlook is the only current evaluation.

heading: What would move the figure
text: Marine protected areas, and protected areas or OECMs in the northern mountains, would close the gaps that the land headline hides.

heading: Summary
text: Morocco covers 33.70% of its land (Western Sahara excluded): 2.13% in protected areas and 31.56% in 338 OECMs. The sea is at 0.33%, 83,470 km² short of 30%.

heading: The OECM question
text: 221 permanent hunting reserves, all reported in 2021 under collaborative governance, supply 29.7 points of the land figure. None has an effectiveness evaluation. Their biodiversity outcomes need documenting before they carry a national 30x30 claim.

heading: Ecosystems and inland waters
text: Mediterranean woodlands and forests are 14.9% covered and the argan woodlands 20.8%. Lakes and wetlands are 21.6% covered; the Saharan Upwelling marine ecoregion 0.1%.

heading: Key Biodiversity Areas
text: The 67 KBAs average 58.5%, but only 24.2% from protected areas. The largest uncovered KBA areas are the two Canary Current shelf sites offshore.

heading: Governance and effectiveness
text: 88% of covered land is under shared governance. No evaluation is less than five years old.

heading: What would move the figure
text: Designating the 42 proposed sites in the WDPA, among them the new natural parks and five marine protected areas, would raise the protected-area figure and start to close the marine gap.

heading: Summary
text: Libya's five WDPA sites, all points, cover 0.13% of its land and 0.63% of its sea. Reaching 30% would take 486,952 km² on land and 104,956 km² at sea.

heading: A data gap more than a protection gap
text: The NBSAP 2023–2030 describes 11 reserves by 2010 and 30 sites announced in 2021, none of them in the WDPA. Every figure here rests on circles drawn around five coordinates; El Nagaza alone gives 84% of the land figure and all of the sea figure.

heading: Ecosystems and inland waters
text: Seven of nine land ecoregions, 96% of the land, have no protection; 0.3% of lakes and wetlands and none of the salt pans are covered.

heading: Key Biodiversity Areas
text: Sixteen of 18 KBAs have no coverage; the average is 0.32%.

heading: What would move the figure
text: Reporting the national network to UNEP-WCMC with boundaries is the single most useful step for Libya's Target 3 reporting.

heading: Summary
text: Egypt covers 11.24% of its land and 3.62% of its sea with the Halaib Triangle excluded, and 12.81% and 4.62% with it included. The national target is 20% of protected areas and OECMs by 2030.

heading: Halaib and proposed sites
text: Gebel Elba National Park lies largely in Halaib. Thirteen protected areas proposed in 1999, 56,941 km² including the Qattara Depression, are excluded until designated; they would bring land coverage to about 17%.

heading: Ecosystems and inland waters
text: The Red Sea mountains and coast are the best covered; the Nile valley and delta are almost unprotected (Nile Delta ecoregion 0.6%, riverine wetlands 0.2%). Lakes and wetlands are 5.0% covered.

heading: Key Biodiversity Areas
text: The 33 KBAs average 35.2%; 8 are complete and 15 have none, including the Upper Nile and El Qasr desert.

heading: Governance and effectiveness
text: 47.9% of covered land has no governance type, mainly El-Gelf El-Keber. Only Wadi Al-Hitan has a current evaluation.

heading: What would move the figure
text: Designating the proposed sites, protecting stretches of the Nile and its wetlands, and filling governance types in the WDPA.
